claim: Direct stochastic hill climbing on the step heights (block, single-point, and smoothing perturbations with occasional uphill moves) from the uniform start raises R from 2/3 to 0.8578, the best result of generation 1. The winning shape is smooth and unimodal (0% zeros, max/mean 2.81) with its autoconvolution peak near the center (0.488) and a markedly flatter top than a triangle: 16.5%/37.7% of kno

Coarse-to-fine multiscale hill climbing (N=32 up to 512, upsampling between levels) reaches R=0.8430, second best in generation 1, and beats the single-level N=256 climb (0.8080, p0007) despite the finer grid. The resulting f*f is asymmetric (peak at 0.705 of support) with 20.8%/43.3% of knots within 1%/5% of max.

A single-level N=256 block-multiplicative annealed hill climb from uniform already lifts R to 0.8080 (+0.141 over 2/3), confirming uniform is not a local maximum under block perturbations. The shape stays positive (0% zeros) with max/mean 1.89 and a centered f*f peak (0.500).

Low-dimensional cosine-mode parametrization h = max(0, 1 + a1 cos + a2 cos2 + a3 cos3) with a coarse grid plus coordinate descent only reaches R=0.7239, far below free-form hill climbing (0.858, p0004). The 3-mode family is too rigid: it forces 31% zeros and a sharply peaked f*f (only 3.2% of knots within 1% of max), so the flat-top regime is unreachable in this basis.

Gaussian-bump starts plus random multiplicative coordinate ascent at large N (up to 1200) reach only R=0.7163, and multi-resolution coordinate-wise climbing from bump starts at N up to 3200 reaches only 0.7396. Both are dominated by block hill climbing at N~42-512 (0.858, p0004; 0.843, p0006), indicating that very fine grids and smooth-bump seeds trap the search in pointed-autoconvolution basins r

The best shapes so far are smooth, positive, and unimodal with max/mean ~2.5-2.8 and a near-centered f*f peak, but p0006's asymmetric peak (0.705) at N=512 suggests asymmetry may help. Worth testing: does explicitly penalizing the curvature of f*f near its maximum (or seeding from p0004's shape and refining at higher N) push R above 0.86, and is the true optimum symmetric or asymmetric?

Adaptive multiplicative/additive/smoothing hill climbing with annealing acceptance, step-size decay/reset and resolution resampling from p0004's shape raises R from 0.857842 to 0.862002 (+0.0042) at N=58, the best result of generation 2. The winning f*f is flatter-topped than p0004's (40.2% of knots within 1% of max vs 37.7%) and its peak sits off-center at 0.543 of support, with max/mean height 3

Exact-gradient projected ascent from p0004's shape produced zero improvement (0.857842, +0.000000, unchanged) in 25.5 s CPU at N=42. The analytic gradient is correct but the shape was already at a local optimum under sum-normalization, so gradient ascent cannot escape it; the crude hill climb's value was exploration, not precision.

Restricting to symmetric heights (N/2 free coordinates, mirror-expanded) collapsed R from 0.857842 to 0.714235 (-0.1436) at N=64. The symmetric start (0.5*(h+h[::-1])) is nearly flat (max/mean 1.32) and its f*f is sharply peaked (only 2.3% of knots within 1% of max), so the symmetry constraint plus the symmetrized start landed in a bad basin; the claimed no-loss symmetry reduction is not usable wi

Coarse random symmetric search (30000 draws of 6-parameter mirrored N=12 shapes) followed by exact-gradient ascent on the top 30 seeds and polish at N=72/96 reaches R=0.860261 (+0.0024 over p0004) at N=42, second best of generation 2. The coarse basin search found a shape with max/mean 3.01 and f*f peak at 0.548 of support, confirming that a global coarse search plus local polish is competitive wi

Geometric resolution growth (256 to 2048) with a final coordinate-wise refinement pass on p0006's shape raises R from 0.842977 to 0.843833 (+0.00086) at N=2048, a marginal gain. The high-N result (f*f peak at 0.695 of support, only 22% of knots within 1% of max) remains well below the small-N results, so spending budget at high N does not close the gap to N~40-60 shapes.

The best shapes (p0010 0.8620, p0011 0.8603) both have off-center f*f peaks (0.543 and 0.548 of support) and max/mean height ~3.0-3.2, while p0004's centered peak (0.488) scored lower. Worth testing whether explicitly penalizing centered peaks or seeding asymmetric shapes at small N (40-60) pushes R past 0.865, and whether the optimum is genuinely asymmetric or just a basin artifact.

The winning shape is markedly different: 25% zero heights, max/mean 6.50, f*f peak at 0.838 of support, and 32.1% of f*f knots within

High-resolution refinement of a poor basin is wasted: the f*f top stays sharp (only 10.5% of knots within 1% of max, peak at 0.515). Resolution is not the lever; basin

Applying p0017's smoothed-max surrogate (p=8..512) to p0019's flatter basin, resampled to N=40 (60% budget) and N=72 (40%), produced zero gain: R stayed at 0.867286 (the start unchanged, N=72). p0019's basin is a local optimum under the surrogate too, so p0019's flat top does not combine with p0017's escape mechanism to beat p0017.

Adding an N-search phase (trying several step counts, keeping best true R) on top of p0017's surrogate climb gained only +0.000026 (0.877702 -> 0.877727) at N=40; the search stayed at N=40. Fixed-N=40 was not the binding limitation, so varying N alone does not improve the surrogate basin.

Growing resolution to N=8192 with a p-ramp surrogate then true-R polish from p0012's shape gained only +0.0005 (0.843833 -> 0.844333) at N=8192, far below the small-N sparse results (0.878-0.881). High-resolution smooth shapes (max/mean 2.57, 0% zeros) are a much worse regime than sparse small-N shapes; resolution growth does not rescue them.

Adding exact analytic gradient ascent on R (score_and_grad) before hill climbing, alternating resolutions, raised R from 0.862002 to 0.864569 (+0.0026) at N=120. Unlike the earlier zero-gain gradient attempt (F8), gradient ascent here did improve, but the result (0.8646) still trails the surrogate-based sparse shapes (0.878-0.881), so gradient ascent helps locally but does not reach the best basin

Seeding p0022's sparse shape (N=68, 28% zeros, max/mean 4.0) and running deterministic coordinate-wise line search on the smoothed-max surrogate S_p (p=256..16384, then true-R) raised R from 0.881216 to 0.881377 (+0.00016) in 0.21 s CPU. The tiny gain shows p0022 was already near coordinate-wise optimal at N=68, so remaining headroom is not in single-coordinate moves.

Scaling up the sparse-random-chain search that produced p0022 — 10 independent chains at N=24..120 (80% of budget) with sigma in {0.5,0.9,1.3}, then high-p refine and true-R polish — raised R from 0.881216 to 0.883544 (+0.00233), the best result of generation 5. The winning shape is at N=78 with 27% zeros, max/mean 4.12, f*f peak at 0.519 and 13.4% of knots within 0.1% of max (vs 3.65% for p0022):

A second independent implementation (gradient ascent then p-schedule climb and true-R polish) reached 0.882933 (+0.00172) in 27.6 s. Gradient descent on the smooth surrogate is an effi

Applying the staged smoothed-p then true-R climb with adaptive N targets to p0019's flatter basin (N=72, 42.8% of f*f knots within 1% of max) produced zero gain: R stayed at 0.867286, the start unchanged, after 27 s CPU. p0019's basin is a local optimum for this move set, consistent with F21's earlier zero-gain result on the same basin.

Adding a smoothing move and optional SA temperature to p0023's top-k-mean climb, with tighter phase allocation toward true-R polish, gained only +0.000007 (0.878173 -> 0.878180) at N=40. The top-k surrogate basin is essentially saturated; extra move types and annealing do not unlock further gains there.

p0031's best shape (N=78, 27% zeros, max/mean 4.12, f*f peak at 0.519, 13.4% of knots within 0.1% of max) is qualitatively different from p0017's dense basin and was only briefly polished after the chain search. Worth testing: does exact-gradient L-BFGS-B on S_p (which gained +0.0012 on p0022 in 0.43 s) applied to p0031's shape, or many more chains at N=70..100, push past 0.884? The sparse-basin f

A coarse asymmetric block parametrization (K=12 free block heights, width 6, N=72) searched by L-BFGS-B multistart on S_p plus full-dim refinement and true-R polish produced zero gain: R stayed at 0.883544 (start unchanged) at N=78 after 17.5 s CPU. Coarse blocks cannot reach the sparse fine-grained structure; the sparse basin is not an artifact of the surrogate's local geometry.

Replacing p0018's finite-difference/inner-loop gradient with the exact analytic score+gradient (single convolution) and a geometric refinement ladder up to N=2016 raised R from 0.859844 to 0.861563 (+0.00172). The result is dense (0% zeros, max/mean 3.20) with an off-center f*f peak at 0.786 of support — still far below the small-N sparse results (0.883), confirming high-resolution dense shapes ar

Spending the budget on heavy fixed-N refinement of p0030's shape (high-p surrogate then true-R polish, brief nearby-N exploration, final polish) raised R from 0.881377 to 0.883541 (+0.00216) at N=68, essentially matching p0031's chain-found 0.883544. The f*f peak moved to 0.662 of support and 15.3% of knots sit within 0.1% of max — a flatter top than p0031's 13.4%.

Heavy fixed-N refinement of p0031's own shape (main driver), then brief nearby-N exploration and a final polish, raised R from 0.883544 to 0.883671 (+0.000127) at N=78 — the best result so far, but a marginal gain. The shape stayed sparse (23.1% zeros, max/mean 4.12) while the f*f peak shifted from 0.519 to 0.442 of support, showing the peak location is not tightly pinned within the basin.

Replacing p0035's random multiplicative/additive climb with deterministic golden-section cyclic coordinate descent over the p-ladder (256..16384) then true R, plus pairwise moves, raised R from 0.883671 to 0.887434 (+0.00376) at N=78 in 13.5 s CPU — the largest single gain in generations 5-7 and the new best. Deterministic coordinate line search descends further into the same basin than the stocha

Doubling resolution from N=78 to N=156 (np.interp resample) and running p0035's fixed-N p-schedule refinement there raised R from 0.883671 to 0.883926 (+0.00026) at N=173. The gain is small and far below p0040's same-N deterministic descent, so the N=78 discretization was only weakly limiting: the basin is mostly resolution-saturated, and the extra knots buy ~0.0003, not a new regime.

Applying p0035's heavy fixed-N p-surrogate refinement plus nearby-N trials to p0032's independent basin (f*f peak at 0.346, 14.7% zeros) gained only +0.000094 (0.883541 -> 0.883635) at N=68 in 25 s. p0032's basin is essentially saturated under this recipe, unlike p0035's, which the same recipe later lifted by +0.0038 once the inner climb was made deterministic. Basin identity matters more than rec

Interleaving analytic-gradient L-BFGS-B polish on the smooth-max surrogate with the random climb on p0035 gained only +0.000020 (0.883671 -> 0.883691) at N=78 in 28 s, and the f*f peak moved to 0.647 of support. Gradient polish on the surrogate does not escape or deepen this basin, consistent with earlier zero-gain L-BFGS-B attempts on p0031 (F31) and p0019 (F21).

Replacing p0035's ±N exploration with a smoothing/densifying denoise phase (moving-average smoothing then denser resample, keep if better) gained only +0.000004 (0.883671 -> 0.883675) at N=78. Smoothing-then-densifying does not improve the sparse shape; the sparse structure (16-22% zeros, max/mean ~4.1) is load-bearing and smoothing destroys it.

p0040's deterministic golden-section coordinate descent beat the stochastic climb by +0.0038 on p0035's basin, while the same stochastic climb on p0032's basin (p0042) and gradient polish on p0035 (p0043) both stalled. Worth testing: does deterministic coordinate descent also unlock p0032's basin and p0039's N=156 shape, and does alternating deterministic coordinate descent with the p-ramp at high

Extending p0040's deterministic coordinate descent past its 13.5 s cutoff — adding an outer deadline loop with random-order true-score sweeps, pairwise golden blend+scale moves, and periodic single-index perturbations with p=16384 re-sweeps — gained only +0.000009 (0.887434 -> 0.887443) at N=78 in 27 s. p0040's shape was already converged; the residual budget and extra move types buy nothing on th

Running p0040's deterministic descent at higher resolution (resample to N=156/117/78 with p-ladder up to 65536) from p0040's shape gained only +0.000001 (0.887434 -> 0.887435), and the best kept shape stayed at N=78. The N=156 discretization headroom that p0039's weak stochastic climb left untested is not real for this basin: the deterministic descent finds nothing at finer N.

Upsampling p0042's shape by factors 2/3/4 before the p-schedule polish gained only +0.000005 (0.883635 -> 0.883640) at N=68, with the f*f peak unchanged at 0.662. Upsampling-then-climb does not escape the current-N local optimum on this basin, consistent with the smoothing/densifying failure (F41).

A time-ramped p-sweep with per-round perturbation and final multiplicative coordinate polish on true R, applied to p0033's basin, gained only +0.000049 (0.883537 -> 0.883587) at N=88 in 28 s. Stochastic p-ramp polish on an already-refined basin is essentially a no-op, matching the pattern that only deterministic coordinate descent produces large gains (F37).

Multi-resolution L-BFGS polishing on a smooth p-norm max surrogate, upsampling p0002's cosine-mode start to N=2048, gained only +0.000004 (0.723882 -> 0.723887) in 0.78 s. The low-dimensional cosine family remains a dead end: gradient polish cannot lift it above ~0.724, far below free-form results.

Replacing single-coordinate and adjacent-pair multiplicative moves with rigid-window scaling (shared multiplier over windows of size 3/5/9/17, golden-section, interleaved with coord/pair sweeps) in the deterministic p-ladder descent on p0049's N=136 shape raised R from 0.887774 to 0.888868 (+0.00109), the best result of generation 9. Running a full p-ladder deterministic coord/pair descent (p=512..131072 then true R) at N=136 on p0049's shape gained only +0.000024 (0.887774 -> 0.887798) in 16 s. More converged sweeps of the same single/pair move set at fixed N do not pay; the N=136 shape is locally converged under those moves, so gains must come from a richer move set or a different surrogate.

Swapping the p-norm max surrogate for a mean-of-top-k surrogate (frac ladder 0.20 down to 0.004) inside the deterministic descent on p0049's N=136 shape gained only +0.000155 (0.887774 -> 0.887929) in 26 s, far below the +0.0005 predicted and below the window-move gain (+0.00109, p0055). Surrogate bias toward the flat top is not what limits the N=136 polish; the move set is.

Broadening the nearby-N exploration to scale factors 0.75/1.5/2/2.5x around p0049's N=136 shape gained only +0.000110 (0.887774 -> 0.887884). Rescaling N and re-descending does not escape the fixed-N optimum; consistent with earlier upsampling-then-climb failures.

Transplanting the deterministic coordinate+pair golden descent through a p-ladder (plus rescaled-N trials and true-R polish) onto p0030's sparse basin (N=68, 28% zeros) raised R from 0.881377 to 0.883508 (+0.00213) at N=102. This confirms the deterministic descent generalizes across basins, but the result stays well below the p0042/p0049 basin's 0.8878-0.8889, so basin choice still dominates.

Adding a densification phase (resample to higher N, refine each) to p0038's shape produced zero gain: R stayed at 0.883675 (N=78) after 27.6 s. Densify-then-refine does not escape the fixed-resolution optimum, matching the smoothing/densifying failure on p0035.
